title.narrative: Tajikistan Strengthening Water and Irrigation Management Project

description.narrative: The development objective of Strengthening Water and Irrigation Management Project for Tajikistan is to: (i) strengthen capacity for water resources planning and irrigation management in Tajikistan and (ii) improve performance of selected irrigation schemes in the Vakhsh and Zarafshon river basins. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Water Sector Reform and Institutional Strengthening, has the following sub-components: (i) Strengthening national and basin-level water resources policy and planning; and (ii) Improving irrigation planning and management. 2) The second component, Irrigation Scheme Improvements, has the following sub-components: (i) Improving large-scale irrigation schemes; and (ii) Improving small- and medium-scale irrigation schemes. 3) The third component, Project Management, aims to support incremental operating costs for project execution, including project management, management of social and environmental issues, financial management (FM), procurement, contract administration, project reporting, and monitoring and evaluation (M&E).

The project development objective is to: (i) strengthen capacity for water resources planning and irrigation management in Tajikistan and (ii) improve performance of selected irrigation schemes in the Vakhsh and Zarafshon river basins.

condition.narrative: Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.1. The Recipient shall no later than two (2) months after the Effective Date,establish and thereafter maintain, throughout Project implementation, a Project Steering Committee with a mandate, functions, andresources satisfactory to the Association, to be responsible for overall coordination, guidance, and oversight.

The Recipient, through MoEWR, shall maintain, throughout Project implementation, aPIU with a mandate, functions, and resources, and staff in adequate numbers and with qualifications, experience, and terms ofreference satisfactory to the Association, responsible for implementation of Parts 1.1 and 3(i) of the Project.

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.3.The Recipient, through MoEWR, shall no later than one (1) month after the EffectiveDate, recruit to the PIU, a project manager/coordinator, a financial management specialist, a procurement specialist, and a socialspecialist, all with qualifications, experience, and terms of reference satisfactory to the Association.

The Recipient shall cause ALRI to, no later than three (3) month after the EffectiveDate, establish and thereafter maintain a support unit for the irrigation management information system implemented under Part 1.2of the Project, with a composition, mandate, and resources satisfactory to the Association.

title.narrative: Value of production in targeted large schemes
Energy intensity of water delivered in targeted large schemes (reduction)

comment.narrative:
Baseline values of energy intensity of irrigation delivery in the Vakhsh and Shurobod systems and their sub-systems are expected to be derived based on the energy sector audit by the end of 2024. Indicative values of energy intensity in targeted irrigation subsystems have been derived in the feasibility study for Vakhsh and Shurobod irrigation systems and will be reported upon validation in the next ISR.
15 April, 2025 Energy savings at the pumping stations in the Vakhsh and Shurobod canal systems will be determined after the completion of repair and rehabilitation work at these facilities.

April 15, 2025 The Action Plan on Improving the Role of Women in the Water Sector was adopted by the PIU. This document was developed with the support of a WB consultant and includes a number of measures and actions both within the project and at the policy development level. At the same time, the PIU is working with the Human Resources Department of the Water Resources Development Agency to improve gender performance.

The project has already surpassed the 20% gender representation target in both the RBO and RBC structures. The WIS unit under MEWR has also met and exceeded its 10% target. Once the NWC appointments are finalized, gender representation in that body will be assessed accordingly. Overall, this indicator is on track and demonstrates strong progress towards gender mainstreaming in water governance.

One of the key Project implementation indicators is under the constant attention of the PMU management. PMU specialists, together with representatives of the NGO Nakukor, created a short mobile number (3553) for complaints and appeals, which operates throughout the Project implementation area. Project beneficiaries can call this number daily with their inquiries and complaints. PMU specialists, together with representatives of relevant organizations, also held meetings with beneficiaries throughout the Project implementation area and provided them with information materials containing full details on the complaint and appeal submission mechanism in Tajik and Uzbek. Information boards, complaint boxes, and banners have also been installed in all these subsystems. Since the beginning of the project, more than 24 complaints and appeals have been received, all of which have been fully resolved.

This indicator tracks the functioning and effectiveness of the project GRM, and so is relevant to citizen engagement. The indicator is the percentage of registered grievances that are satisfactorily resolved with two months of receipt.
April 15, 2025 The PMU specialists and Nakukor civil society representatives have set up a 24/7 grievance hotline (tel: 3553) across the project area. They have held meetings with project beneficiaries to share information and materials about the grievance mechanism process in Tajik and Uzbek. Information boards, complaint boxes, and banners have also been installed throughout the subsystems. Since the project began, over 19 complaints have been received and resolved.

In the L-2 Sargakh Canal Subsystem- (11) Repair of the L-2 Sargah dam, (12) PK 104 channel GMK, (13) PK 143 channel GMK

title.narrative: Selected small/medium schemes rehabilitated for enhanced performance

comment.narrative: PMU developed criteria for selecting priority sites in the upper reaches of the Vakhsh and Zarafshon river basins. Sites meeting these criteria were included in the current Project for implementation. Restoration work is currently ongoing at these sites. Upon completion, the PMU will conduct an assessment to confirm the results achieved and document the infrastructure improvements.

title.narrative: Area with improved water delivery in targeted large schemes

comment.narrative:
The baseline study determining the baseline  analysis for targeted large schemes - Vakhsh Main Canal and Shurobod Canal is launched. A follow up study will be conducted in 2025 to track progress against the Intermediate Target 1.
15 April, 2025 The rehabilitation of 4 subsystems and the associated area with improved irrigation is as follows: (i) Central Channel Subsystem, total land area - 4929 ha, (ii) October Channel Subsystem, total land area -9527 ha, (iii) Sargakh Canal Subsystem, total land area - 11,699 ha, (iv) Northern branch subsystem, total land area -25,758 ha. Based on data collected from restored facilities, the total area of improved land exceeds 15,000 ha. However, an accurate estimate of the improved land area can only be determined after the entire restoration is complete.

title.narrative: Area with improved water delivery in targeted large schemes

comment.narrative: Since the Project only plans to restore irrigation facilities, the area of irrigated land is only improving, not expanding. According to the data obtained, in those subsystems where restoration work has already been completed, farmers, according to surveys conducted by Unit specialists, received the required amount of water throughout the irrigation season, meeting the crops' water requirements, without problems and in a timely manner. These indicators were achieved thanks to the activities implemented within the Project; more than 23 construction contracts have been signed to date. To determine this indicator, it is first necessary to conduct remote sensing of the land in the selected systems to obtain accurate and reliable data.

title.narrative: Selected major hydraulic structures in target schemes repaired

comment.narrative: As part of this project, more than 40 major hydraulic structures are being repaired and restored in the 6th subsystem of the Vakhsh and Shurabad Canals, which is one of the main issues facing these subsystems. If the water distribution structures are fully operational, this will reduce water losses and ensure proper water distribution. The list of restored facilities has been fully compiled.

title.narrative: Selected vulnerable schemes resilient to climate extremes

comment.narrative: April 15, 2025 Irrigation facilities that are likely to be seriously damaged during natural disasters and require extensive repair and relocation are located in the Upper Vakhshi River basin and partially in the Lower Vakhshi River basin. In the Lower Vakhshi River basin 3 facilities have been repaired and restored. These include: (1) Rehabilitation of the Aqueduct at PK 98+33 L-2 Sargah, (2) PK 209 Gulistan Canal, and (3) PK 104+65 GMK Canal, all of which are part of the L-2 Sargakh channel subsystem. In the Upper Vakhshi River basin, rehabilitation work has begun on the Nushor, Sari Pul and Gulama canals.

title.narrative: Selected vulnerable schemes resilient to climate extremes

comment.narrative: This indicator focuses on irrigation structures that are susceptible to serious damage during natural disasters and require repair and relocation. These irrigation structures are planned in the Upper Vakhsh basin and partially in the Lower Vakhsh. To achieve this indicator, the Project is to implement the following contracts, including: SWIM-CW-ICB-001 Rehabilitation of the VMC Subsystem of the Kumsangir Canal, SWIM-CW-NCB-08 Rehabilitation of the Shurabad Canal System, SWIM-CW-NCB-023 Rehabilitation of the Fathabad, Kuglik, and Surkhkul Canals, SWIM-CW-NCB-024 Rehabilitation of the Simtosh and Sartalo Canals and the Karasoy Pumping Station, the Kashkateraku Pumping Station, and SWIM-CW-NCB-010 Rehabilitation of the Dangara Irrigation Tunnel (DIT).L-13.8 km. Restoration work has begun in full swing at the above-mentioned sites.

title.narrative: Value of production in targeted large schemes

comment.narrative: Based on this indicator and data collected by the Statistics Agency, it was established that the cost of agricultural production in the specified subsystems, where repair, restoration, and reconstruction work was carried out as part of the Project, has improved compared to previous years. The change in the cost of agricultural production compared to previous periods indicates increased efficiency in production processes and more efficient use of water and energy resources, which has led to a significant improvement in cost indicators in these subsystems. Analytical calculations have currently been conducted for four subsystems where work has been fully completed. Detailed analytical results will be presented in the 2025 consolidated report.

title.narrative: Pump stations in target schemes modernized
Energy intensity of water delivered in targeted large schemes (reduction)

comment.narrative: This indicator includes the collection and systematization of baseline information on the VMC and ShMC pumping stations, conducted prior to the commencement of the Project. This will enable a subsequent comparative analysis of the pumping stations' condition and an assessment of the improvements achieved after the completion of the work. Key energy efficiency indicators for pumping stations in the Vakhsh and Shurabad canal systems will be calculated upon completion of a full range of repair and restoration measures at these facilities. This indicator is expected to provide a more accurate assessment of the current condition and efficiency of the pumping stations based on an energy audit conducted by an international organization. Restoration work has been completed at six pumping stations.

title.narrative: Pump stations in target schemes modernized

comment.narrative: To date, three contracts have been signed under the Project, covering the overhaul and reconstruction of three pumping stations in the Northern Branch subsystem, two pumping stations in the Sargakh L-2 subsystem, and five pumping stations in the Kumsangir subsystem. As a result of these projects, the work has been fully completed and five pumping stations have been commissioned. Restoration work has now begun on one pumping station located in the Kumsangir subsystem.

title.narrative: Selected small/medium schemes rehabilitated for enhanced performance

comment.narrative: April 15, 2025 The rehabilitation of small and medium-sized irrigation facilities is planned in the Upper Vakhsh River basin and the Zarafshan River basin. In the upper Vakhsh River basin, work has begun on 7 facilities. In the Zarafshan River basin, work on the 1st water pumping station is expected to begin.
April 15, 2025 Tender documents have been fully prepared and submitted to the World Bank for review by the PMU specialists.

The international IMIS consultant and the national ICT consultant from the ALRI PMU, with the assistance of World Bank consultants, prepared tender documentation and cost estimates for the following packages: "Design, supply, installation, and commissioning of the irrigation information management system (IMIS ) software" and "IT equipment for the irrigation information management system (IMIS )." The IMIS consultant also supports the ALRI and the PMU in evaluating companies' technical proposals and negotiating contracts. The hiring of a coordinator to support the implementation of the IMIS is planned. The Asian Development Bank Project also continues to develop a financial and commercial management module, and to date, the following work has been completed: field surveys were conducted in the Yavan district, field data export was completed, a temporary MS Access database was created, equipment was purchased, the necessary software was identified and installed, and web-based IMIS

title.narrative: Irrigation energy audit and tariff review complete

comment.narrative: To achieve this target, a contract was signed with an international consulting company on February 9, 2024, for "Consulting Services for the Development of a Land Reclamation and Irrigation Development Strategy" (Contract No. SWIM-CS-QCBS-03). The company submitted a sector energy audit report and a sector baseline assessment report, which are currently under review by the World Bank. A roundtable discussion with members of the Interagency Working Group on the Development of the Irrigation Strategy and other stakeholders is scheduled for October 24, 2025, to review the sector energy audit report. Draft reports, "Review of Tariffs and Subsidies for Irrigation Services with Recommendations on Tariff Regimes" and "Draft Concept for the Development of the Irrigation and Land Reclamation Sector," were also prepared and are currently under review by stakeholders.

In the Main Vakhsh Canal and the Main Shurabad Canal, full preparatory work has been carried out and the transition to a new form of management will begin on January 1, 2026.

title.narrative: National and basin-level water planning institutions established and resourced

comment.narrative:
All three institutional bodies—RBO, RBC, and NWC—have been formally established and are progressing toward full operationalization. The first formal meetings of the RBC and NWC are scheduled within the current reporting period, ensuring alignment with project milestones and contributing to the achievement of this indicator.
No progress reported against the Intermediate Target 2.

title.narrative: ALRI and WUAs strengthened to enable effective management of targeted large schemes

comment.narrative: Complete information on the inventory of irrigation systems and the development of a GIS layer was collected by an international consulting company and transferred to the Irrigation Management Information System (IMIS) department of the ALRI . Once the IMIS is equipped with the necessary equipment, full data entry into the information system is planned. Work is simultaneously ongoing on developing a Land Reclamation and Irrigation Development Strategy, and once completed, the document will be approved by the National Water Council. Activities have also been initiated as part of the audit of Water User Associations, which are actively continuing with the participation of an international consulting company. Based on the information collected for this indicator, it can be confidently stated that work in this area is progressing vigorously, and achieving this indicator is entirely possible by the end of the first irrigation season of 2027.

title.narrative: ALRI and WUAs strengthened to enable effective management of targeted large schemes

comment.narrative:
No progress reported against the Intermediate Target 1 and Intermediate Target 2. 
The development of the GIS-inventory for irrigation infrastructure has been completed and handed over to the IMIS unit of ALRI. The IMIS package is going under bidding, and the National Irrigation Strategy is under development.

title.narrative: National and basin-level water planning institutions established and resourced

comment.narrative:
The progress under the Intermediate Target 1 is described as follows: The Vakhsh River Basin Organization has been created as a Department of Vakhsh River Basin under the Ministry of Energy and Water Resources, with the main office located in Bokhtar. Vakhsh River Basin Council members have been appointed with the first meeting held by the MEWR. No activities to support capacity of the newly established wing of the MEWR have been conducted yet. The National Water Council has been established, but is yet to hold its first meetings.
No progress reported against the Intermediate Target 2.

No activities have started in support of the NWS, RBO and RBC staff training.
April 15, 2025 The project team collaborated with MEWR by monitoring 5 training sessions to identify gaps in the existing 8 training modules developed by the TRIGER Project and to collect data for analysis. Based on these findings, the PIU plans to work with MEWR starting in June 2025 to revise and improve the modules where deficiencies were found.

While formal training for NWC and RBC members is scheduled for the upcoming period, fundamental steps have been taken to ensure a structured and needs-based approach. The RBO has already commenced its training program, demonstrating early progress towards institutional capacity development under this indicator.

April 15, 2025 The RBO Office renovation and equipment acquisition were delayed due to issues with allocation of premises. A joint field visit on April 22-23, 2025, resolved this by selecting a new location at picket #33 in Levakand district, near Bokhtar city. RBO staff are now responsible for obtaining formal authorization from the district administration for construction.

While physical construction has not yet begun, the fundamental administrative processes are actively progressing. The timely resolution of land allocation will enable the subsequent implementation of infrastructure and equipment-related activities under this indicator.
